account:
Today is day 1, shortly after nine. I read my appointment book this morning: mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea at the east-dock cottage at fifteen, and Builder's office report at sixteen thirty. Neighbour said Freight wanted to know when to expect me and would be at the east landing this morning; she now intends to tell him ten. I do not yet know of any problem with the grain.

Builder is conducting an authorized preventive inspection of town hall doors, bridge decking, and the east ferry landing. The agreed fee is two emeralds on delivery of written findings, with no repairs authorized. He reported no visible bridge defects and a normally functioning entrance door. Nothing so far establishes an urgent safety problem. The unusual difficulty has been communication and writing materials: Builder repeatedly missed the landing clarification and has no book or funds; Secretary found only signed books in the office chest. I authorized one emerald separately for a writable office book so Secretary can transcribe his findings for his review. I successfully handed her that emerald and saw her holding it, but then heard her ask for the money as though she had not received it. My following explanation reached nobody, and she is now out of sight. This appears to be a coordination problem, not evidence of misconduct; I should confirm receipt when we next meet rather than pay twice.

Baker came asking whether town hall needed bread for gatherings. No gathering or bread order has been confirmed, and I authorized none. Otherwise people appear to be moving through their morning routines. My immediate obligation is to reach the mill for ten and learn what its grain inspection reveals.
